newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica sees more sugar production, lower earnings.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica sees more sugar production, lower earnings.

text.p: Jamaica's sugar industry expects to produce nearly eight percent more sugar this year but earn less for it as a result of currency fluctuations, officials said Wednesday.

The 1997 projected production of 256,000 tonnes is 7.7 percent more than the 237,643 tonnes produced in 1996. Exports are expected to reach 175,000 tonnes, nearly all of which will go to the European Union.
Karl James, general manager of Jamaica Cane Products Sales, which handles all of Jamaica's exports, said the sector expects to earn $100.6 million from exports, down slightly from last year.
He said the decrease would be due to a 10 percent price reduction caused by the strengthening of the pound against the U.S. dollar.
This year's production target would see Jamaica utilizing 73 percent of its 350,000-tonne production capacity at its eight sugar factories.
James said the industry aims to achieve 85-90 percent capacity and reduce cropping time from ten to seven months by 1999.
